name: Residence Permit for Higher Education Studies

requirements.blocker_text: Requires final admission to full-time studies (30 credits/semester at university, or 20+ teaching hours/week for other programs).
requirements.fix_path: Secure admission to a Swedish institution.

requirements.blocker_text: Requires SEK 10,656/month in personal funds (bank savings, scholarship, sponsorship, employment, or student loan), plus SEK 4,440/month per spouse/partner and SEK 2,664/month per child, reduced if free food/housing is provided.
Required for studies under 1 year, if not registering in Sweden's population register; must cover emergency/other medical care, hospitalization, and emergency dental care.

outcome.duration_length: 1-2 years depending on institution, never exceeding study duration or passport validity

sources.title: Swedish Migration Agency -- Apply for a residence permit for studies at higher education: financial thresholds, insurance, 1-2 year duration, 15hr/week work cap for permits granted after 11 June 2026

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Sweden). work_rights modeled 'restricted' rather than 'none': bachelor's/master's students with permits granted after 11 June 2026 may work up to 15 hours/week, with exceptions for internships, student representation, research roles, and summer employment (June-August) -- a real, recent liberalization worth flagging, in the same reform wave that tightened work-permit salary thresholds elsewhere. Doctoral students and researchers are treated as a distinct, more favorable category under the 2026 reforms (faster PR access, extended post-study employment) -- not modeled as a separate file here given time constraints, but flagged as a gap: a dedicated se_researcher_permit.json could be built as a follow-up given how substantively different its rules now are from ordinary higher-education students.
